answer: A bounded-vouch ledger gives each established identity three endorsements per epoch and requires newcomers to gather five distinct vouches. Each identity posts an onyx-denominated bond slashed on failed attestation, so a fake costs five independently bonded backers plus vouch fees; a jetty queue delays withdrawals two epochs, adding lockup and time. A falcon quorum check rejects vouch clusters with excessive overlap, so coordinated rings exhaust shared endorser budgets and correlated slashing exposes the set.
